Subject: High tail latency and dropped events on streaming chat during peak

Hi Ben,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency on the streaming chat channel (WebSocket) around 07:45 PST this morning. Many of our agents reported delayed messages (5-12s) and occasional disconnects; some clients received 502/504s on reconnects. This happened right as a marketing campaign drove a traffic spike — concurrent streams were ~3x our typical peak.

We captured a few traces and logs and attached a sample screenshot of the p99 trace and a small log bundle. Can you confirm if this is on the Redwood side (routing, runtime) or our integration? We need an ETA for mitigation — this is customer-facing and affecting live conversations.

Attaching: p99-trace-0424.png, ingestion-log-0424.zip

Thanks,
Lena Park

Lena — sorry you’re seeing this. We’re treating it as P1. Quick checks so we can triage faster:

- Can you confirm the client concurrency (streams per user) during the spike and whether you were using SSE or WebSocket?
- If you can, reduce concurrency by 20% (or switch to polling short-term) while we investigate — I can walk your engineers through the change.

Interim mitigations we can push from our side:
- Route your traffic to a less-loaded region for the next hour (minor latency overhead for some clients but reduces p99 tail).
- Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for conversation history for Clevershop account (reduces runtime work).

Rishi — any early signal from runtime?

— Grace
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High tail latency and dropped events on streaming chat during peak

Quick technical readout from infra:

- Observed: regional p99 latency increase on hosted streaming nodes (us-west) beginning 2027-04-24T07:38:00-07:00, coincident with a large traffic wave. Error rate (502/503) rose from baseline 0.2% to 3.4% at peak.
- Root cause hypothesis (initial): an interaction between the new continuous-batching path and the session-eviction policy under high concurrency. Batching code fell back to a slower codepath when KV cache hit-rate dropped below threshold; combined with a transient delayed pod scale-up we saw per-request CPU queuing and long tail jitter.
- Evidence: attached p99 traces show request wait time spiking before execution. We also saw increased KV-miss ratios in the same window.

Immediate actions taken:
1) Rolled back the continuous-batching rollout for streaming nodes in us-west at 09:00 PST (partial rollback, targeted).
2) Forced an emergency scale-up of the hosted streaming pool for the Clevershop tenant region.
3) Enabled more aggressive KV caching for Clevershop (account override).

Next steps (in next 2-6 hours):
- Full rollback validation and post-rollback p99 check.
- Deep RCA: reproduce with synthetic load; review batching fallback thresholds; follow-up JIRA created: JIRA-INF-1998.

Attaching: p99-trace-0424.png (snippet), ingestion-log-0424.zip (8MB).

— Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
